# Open Source Game Tier List Makers on GitHub

Here are the notable open source tier list maker projects available on GitHub:

## General-Purpose Tier List Makers

- **[opentierboy](https://github.com/infinia-yzl/opentierboy)** — An open-source, lightweight tier list creator built with TypeScript. Supports custom rankings, pre-made templates, and easy sharing with no account required. (24 stars, 2 forks)

- **[TierListMaker](https://github.com/thenick775/TierListMaker)** — A client-side browser-based tier list maker with drag-and-drop support. Features include drag-to-upload images, reordering within tiers, custom tier colors, image export, and everything stays in the browser (no server uploads, ads, logins, or tracking).

- **[Easy-Tier-List](https://github.com/Akascape/Easy-Tier-List)** — A desktop tier list maker built with Python and CustomTkinter for a modern UI. (17 stars)

- **[Tier-List-Maker](https://github.com/Procedurally-Generated-Human/Tier-List-Maker)** (and its many forks) — A bare-bones, web-based drag-and-drop tier list maker built with plain JavaScript. Several forks have extended it with additional features like image upload and download.

## Game-Specific Tier List Makers

- **[octopath-tier-list-maker](https://github.com/octopath-tier-list-maker/octopath-tier-list-maker.github.io)** — A tier list maker for the Octopath Traveler series, forked from a Fire Emblem tier list maker. Includes detailed documentation on how to adapt the project for other games/franchises.

- **[genshin-tierlist-maker](https://github.com/bxhuynh/genshin-tierlist-maker)** — A Genshin Impact tier list maker built with React and react-beautiful-dnd.

- **[AutoTiers](https://github.com/SuperFamousGuy/AutoTiers)** — An automatic fantasy football tier list generator using FastAPI, with configurable rules and statistical clustering.

## Also Notable

- **[myrtle](https://github.com/Eltik/myrtle)** — An Arknights companion platform that includes a community tier list feature with drag-and-drop editing, versioning, and a permission system, backed by a Rust API server.

If you want something **quick and general-purpose**, `opentierboy` or `TierListMaker` (thenick775) are great starting points. If you want to **build one for a specific game**, the `octopath-tier-list-maker` includes excellent documentation on how to adapt the template for any franchise.

# Octopath Tier List Maker — Template Documentation for Adapting to Other Games

The [Octopath Tier List Maker](https://github.com/octopath-tier-list-maker/octopath-tier-list-maker.github.io) is an open-source project (deployed via GitHub Pages) that was originally forked from a Fire Emblem tier list maker, which itself traces back to a Smash Apps project. The creator has provided detailed documentation on how to adapt it for **other game franchises**.

## How to Make Your Own Tier List Maker

The project structure is designed so that most customization happens in just a few files and folders:

### 1. `editableJs/` Folder (main content to update)
- **`common.js`** — This is where you define the games that appear. The variable `imgGamesFolder` holds three values per game: the folder name in `img/`, the number of images it contains, and the display name shown on the website.
- **`tags.js`** — Optional filtering support. The `imgTags` constant lets you assign tags to individual character images (matched by their image number). This enables users to filter characters on the tier list.

### 2. `img/` Folder
- Create a **parent folder** (e.g., the franchise name), then **individual folders per game** containing character images.
- Images **must be numbered** so the code can correctly match them to tags and game listings. Don't forget to register these folders in `common.js`.

### 3. `index.html`
- Update the **`<head>` tag** with your franchise's link preview description, preview image, page title, and favicon.
- Replace images in the `img` folder to match your franchise.

### 4. `lib/` Folder (minor optional config)
- In **`toolcommon.js`**, you can change the **default game** displayed when the page loads.

### 5. `nav/` Folder
- Contains supporting libraries; generally **not needed** for adapting to other games.

## Key Features Supported

The tier list maker includes these built-in features that carry over to any adapted version:
- **Change Characters** — Add/remove characters from the selection you want to tier.
- **Filter** — Show only characters matching specific tags.
- **Save/Load** — Generate and re-use tier list layouts as shareable text codes.
- **Reset** — Clear the tier list back to default.
- **Change/Revert Layout** — Toggle characters between below or beside the tier list.
- **Dock Tierlist** — Pin the tier list so it stays visible while scrolling.
- **Hide Controls** — Remove tool widgets for a cleaner look.
- **Screenshot** — Generate an image of your completed tier list.

The project is open-source, contributors are welcome, and you're encouraged to fork it to bring tier list makers to other franchises.

### Gap Analysis for Your Project

**No existing project combines all the features you likely need.** Specifically:

1. **No project supports "曙光英雄" (Dawn of Heroes)** -- This is a gap you can fill.
2. **No project elegantly supports multiple MOBA games from a single codebase** -- Most are hardcoded to one game. The closest are the generic tier list makers (opentierboy, classement-client, octopath), but they lack live data integration.
3. **The hok-meta-analyzer architecture is the strongest reference** for your use case: it is lightweight (static HTML + JSON), uses automated scraping via GitHub Actions for daily updates, has bilingual search, URL-shareable state, mobile-first design, and tier categorization (S/A/B/C/D). It proves that a simple scraper-to-JSON pipeline plus a vanilla JS frontend can produce a fully functional tier list dashboard.
4. **statsWR is the best reference for a full-stack approach** (React frontend, Express API, database-backed), but it is heavier and unmaintaned since July 2024.
5. **For visual polish**, opentierboy (TypeScript/React + Tailwind) and classement-client (Angular + SCSS) have the best drag-and-drop UX and export features.
6. **For adaptability to multiple games**, octopath-tier-list-maker provides the best documentation on how to structure a template that can be forked and customized per game.

### Recommended Architecture (Synthesized from Research)

Based on the best patterns across all projects, an ideal architecture for your multi-MOBA tier list dashboard would be:

- **Data Pipeline:** Python + Playwright scrapers (like hok-meta-analyzer) for each game, outputting standardized JSON, automated via GitHub Actions
- **Frontend:** React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS (like opentierboy) for a modern, maintainable UI with drag-and-drop and responsive design
- **Data Format:** Standardized `heroes.json` per game with fields: name, name_cn, image, tier (S/A/B/C/D), win_rate, pick_rate, ban_rate, role, lane
- **Deployment:** Static site (GitHub Pages / Vercel) with JSON loaded via `fetch()` -- no backend server required
- **Multi-Game Support:** Game selector component that swaps the data source and hero roster, keeping the tier display component game-agnostic
